ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, D is the midpoint of AC, and CE $\perp$ AB at point E. If DE = 3 and AE = 5, then what is the length of CE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since CE$\perp$AB, it follows that $\angle$AEC$=90^\circ$. In the right-angled triangle AEC, since point D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AC, and DE=3, it follows that AC=2DE=6. By the Pythagorean theorem, we have $CE=\sqrt{AC^{2}-AE^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{2}-5^{2}}=\sqrt{11}=\boxed{\sqrt{11}}$.
